workload: FD open/fork/wait/close with 32 and 128 files; equal-object nine-pool replay; standard linked images and bounded QEMU boot endpoints. Payload, pool reservation and fixed image are separate boundaries.
assessment: Adopt packed FD entries and the nonrepeating pool counter with release-only retirement ownership. Nine FD blocks save 1152 payload bytes; eight production pool bodies add 64 bytes. No FD page saving in this workload; RPi5 fixed image reservation adds 32768 bytes. Keep empty-chunk retention 1. Accept the safety cost and avoid exhaustive tuning before feature workloads exist.
next_trigger: Before publishing the next completed kernel feature or roadmap stage, especially new pooled objects, process/thread lifetimes, VM or socket behavior, or an allocator/retention/layout change. Use the new feature workload plus existing baselines; repeat cross-OS measurements only if that boundary changes.
